fullPassage: What do you think good design is? Some might assert good design makes products easy to use, while others might say good design is stylish or innovative. There are even some who believe that good design should be as environmentally friendly as possible. All of these are important elements of design. However, there is a new idea called “universal design.” This idea suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty looks and functions. Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people and includes features that make it possible for them to access and use products without any barriers. Now let’s take a look at how universal design is tackling the problem of limited access and reshaping the design of products and services. Universal design suggests that design be as flexible as possible so that it can accommodate diverse needs and a wide range of individual preferences. This could involve providing a variety of options for customization or adding adjustable features to a product. Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk pictured below. Do you notice how they differ from the more common types of scissors, mice, and desks? They are all designed for left-handed people. Without them, about 10% of the world’s population, who are left-handed, would find these simple products difficult to use. The height-adjustable desk is also a good example of a universal design that accommodates a wide range of individual preferences and abilities. If the desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it to the heights they want. If desired, the user can work while standing. A wheelchair user is also able to use the desk at a comfortable height. Universal design also ensures that an environment or product is accessible to everyone. Anyone should be able to use a design regardless of who they are and what they’re capable of, and no one should be excluded. Curb cuts are a good example. Without curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard time navigating the city. Curb cuts eliminate barriers not only for wheelchair users but also for people moving heavy loads or riding bikes. Like curb cuts, automatic doors in public buildings also allow all people to enter without any major problems. Another characteristic of universal design is requiring low physical effort. Universal design seeks to create products that can be used efficiently and comfortably without causing unnecessary fatigue. Undoubtedly, many people have had trouble trying to open a lid of a jar that was stuck. Opening a lid can be a great challenge to people with a weak grip, the elderly, or people with hand or finger impairments. Fortunately, various clever opening devices have been designed. A lever-type door handle, which requires no firm grip or twisting, is also an example that reflects this characteristic of universal design. A door with a lever-type door handle can be opened using an elbow or a closed hand, which benefits people carrying baskets as well as those with limited strength in their hands. Universal design is not limited to the design of physical products or facilities. Universal design pushes for designs in which critical information is conveyed well, regardless of the surrounding environment or the user’s sensory abilities. Information should be conveyed not just through written language but also through universal symbols and audio cues. For instance, when it comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is much easier when they can simply look for the universally recognized restroom symbol rather than trying to interpret the local language. For those with visual or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival times are not only presented on electronic boards but also called out through voice announcements. In elevators, braille, which indicates the floor number, allows individuals with visual impairments to select their desired floor. Additionally, audio announcements confirm the selected floor and tell passengers when the elevator has reached their desired floor. As such, providing information in these diverse forms ensures that everyone can access and understand important information, regardless of language barriers, sensory impairments, etc. Universal design is beneficial to everyone. With universal design, no one needs to put up with unnecessary discomfort. The supporters of universal design suggest that it should be part of every design. Take a look around you. Is there anything that needs improvement so that it can be accessible to more people? If so, why not create a design and bring joy to more people? Read More Universal Design Playground Play is a fundamental aspect of human development that continues all through our lives. Playgrounds serve as a central place for play, but many individuals struggle to fully engage in these spaces due to their restrictive arrangements. Often, playgrounds are designed to satisfy specific types of play or particular age groups, which can leave children who cannot participate in the intended manner feeling excluded. For children with disabilities, play is even more crucial as it offers an opportunity to practice social skills. However, the conventional design of playgrounds does not typically accommodate their needs, either overwhelming or boring them. A visit to a standard playground with children with disabilities can highlight the weaknesses in design that fail to satisfy everyone. Playgrounds should be designed to foster social connections for all ages, provide sensory stimulation, encourage physical exercise, and connect with nature. Achieving this integration is a challenging design task. By involving children with disabilities and their families in the design process and creating friendlier playgrounds, we can acknowledge that play is more than just a source of enjoyment. This approach results in spaces where people of all abilities, ages, and languages can take part in the joy of play. For example, Martin’s Park, designed by Michael Van Valkenburgh Associates, is a universally designed playground. Unusual play structures and a large ship provide endless experiences of play that can engage every child. The various methods of play have different means of access, allowing kids who are able to scramble up hills, while children who can’t walk can use the sloping paths to reach the top. Interpretive signs point out the inclusive routes and elements of the playground. The inclusion of more than 1,000 trees grants children and adults the chance to experience the sensory aspects of plants. Play isn’t just for kids anymore. Senior play spaces and public exercise equipment are being installed around the world. Play spaces for older adults provide health benefits and encourage engagement with their families and community. Hence, playgrounds need to be redesigned as spaces where everyone can enjoy themselves.

questions.passage: Universal design seeks to create products that can be ①<u>used</u> efficiently and comfortably without causing unnecessary fatigue. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② tried → trying: 'have trouble + 동명사(-ing)'이므로 trying
det.analysis:
✅ ① used: 'products that can be used efficiently'에서 제품은 '사용되는' 대상이라 수동태 be used로 적절
❌ ② tried → trying: 'many people have had trouble ___ to open a lid'는 'have trouble + 동명사(-ing)(~하는 데 애를 먹다)' 구문이다. 따라서 trying이 맞다. tried(과거형)는 이 구문에 쓸 수 없다 ← 정답
✅ ③ Opening: 'Opening a lid can be a great challenge'에서 문장의 주어 자리라 동명사(Opening)로 적절
✅ ④ which: 'a lid of a jar that was stuck'가 아니라, 계속적 관계대명사 자리로 앞 명사를 받아 적절
det.tip: have trouble/difficulty + 동명사(-ing): have trouble trying(애를 먹다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ entering → to enter: 'allow + 목적어 + to부정사'이므로 to enter
det.analysis:
✅ ① ensures: 주어 Universal design(단수)에 맞는 단수 동사 ensures로 적절
✅ ② navigating: 'have a hard time navigating the city'에서 'have a hard time + 동명사(-ing)(~하는 데 어려움을 겪다)'로 적절
❌ ③ entering → to enter: 'automatic doors ~ allow all people ___ without any major problems'는 'allow + 목적어(all people) + to부정사'로 '모두가 들어가게 해 준다'는 뜻이다. 따라서 to enter가 맞다 ← 정답
✅ ④ requiring: 'Another characteristic ~ is requiring low physical effort'에서 be동사 뒤 보어 자리로 적절
det.tip: allow + 목적어 + to부정사: allow all people to enter(모두가 들어가게 하다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① require → requires: 계속적 관계대명사 which가 단수 명사 handle을 받으므로 단수 동사 requires
det.analysis:
❌ ① require → requires: 'A lever-type door handle, which ___ no firm grip or twisting'에서 which는 단수 명사 handle을 받는 주격 관계대명사다. 따라서 단수 동사 requires가 맞다 ← 정답
✅ ② opened: 'can be opened using an elbow'에서 문은 '열리는' 대상이라 수동태 be opened로 적절
✅ ③ using: 'can be opened using an elbow'에서 '~을 사용하여'를 나타내는 분사구문으로 적절
✅ ④ conveyed: 'critical information is conveyed well'에서 정보는 '전달되는' 대상이라 수동태로 적절
det.tip: 관계대명사 which + 단수 선행사(handle) → 단수 동사 requires

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ reshape → reshaping: 'is tackling ~ and reshaping'의 병렬 구조이므로 reshaping
det.analysis:
✅ ① includes: 'Universal design takes into account ~ and includes features'에서 takes와 병렬을 이루는 단수 동사 includes로 적절

❌ ③ reshape → reshaping: 'how universal design is tackling the problem ~ and ___ the design'에서 앞의 is tackling과 병렬로 이어지므로 진행형 형태 reshaping이 맞다 ← 정답

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② loose → stuck: 열기 힘든 것은 꽉 '낀(stuck)' 병뚜껑
det.analysis:
✅ ① physical: '적은 신체적(physical) 노력을 요구한다'는 유니버설 디자인의 특징 설명에 적절
❌ ② loose(헐거운) → stuck(꽉 낀): 많은 사람이 열기 힘들어했다는 문맥이므로, 병뚜껑은 '꽉 낀(stuck)' 상태여야 한다. loose(헐거운)면 쉽게 열려 문맥과 반대 ← 정답
✅ ③ great: '뚜껑 열기가 큰(great) 어려움이 될 수 있다'는 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ strength: 레버형 손잡이가 손의 '힘(strength)'이 제한된 사람에게 이롭다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: stuck(꽉 낀) ↔ loose(헐거운)

det.korean: ④ similar → different: 유니버설 디자인은 '서로 다른(different)' 사람들의 다양한 요구를 고려
det.analysis:

Curb cuts eliminate barriers not only for wheelchair users but also for people moving heavy loads or riding bikes.  Like curb cuts, automatic doors in public buildings also allow all people to enter without any major problems.  Another characteristic of universal design is requiring low physical effort.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 유니버설 디자인의 접근성 원칙.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문 'Anyone should be able to use a design regardless of who they are'에서 누구나 사용할 수 있어야 한다고 했으므로 '건강한 사람만'은 불일치
❌ ② 본문 'automatic doors ~ allow all people to enter'에서 모든 사람이 들어갈 수 있다고 했으므로 '허가받은 사람만'은 불일치
❌ ③ 본문 'Another characteristic of universal design is requiring low physical effort.'에서 적은 신체적 노력은 유니버설 디자인의 '특징'이라 했으므로 '관련이 없다'는 불일치
✅ ④ 본문 'Universal design also ensures that an environment or product is accessible to everyone.'와 일치 ← 정답
det.tip: ensures that ~ is accessible to everyone(모두가 이용 가능하도록 보장)이 근거입니다.

ch: 유니버설 디자인은 신체가 건강한 사람만을 위한 것이다.
공공건물의 자동문은 특별한 허가를 받은 사람만 이용할 수 있다.
적은 신체적 노력을 요구하는 것은 유니버설 디자인과 관련이 없다.
유니버설 디자인은 환경이나 제품을 모두가 이용할 수 있도록 보장한다.

questions.passage: Fortunately, various clever opening devices have been ①<u>designed</u>. A lever-type door handle, which requires no firm grip or twisting, is also an example that ②<u>reflects</u> this characteristic of universal design. A door with a lever-type door handle can be ③<u>opened</u> using an elbow or a closed hand, which benefits people ④<u>carry</u> baskets as well as those with limited strength in their hands.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ carry → carrying: 명사 people을 뒤에서 꾸미는 현재분사이므로 carrying
det.analysis:
✅ ① designed: 'opening devices have been designed'에서 장치는 '만들어지는' 대상이라 수동태 have been designed로 적절
✅ ② reflects: 'an example that reflects this characteristic'에서 that은 단수 선행사 example을 받으므로 단수 동사 reflects로 적절
✅ ③ opened: 'can be opened using an elbow'에서 문은 '열리는' 대상이라 수동태 be opened로 적절
❌ ④ carry → carrying: 'benefits people ___ baskets'에서 baskets를 든 people을 뒤에서 꾸며야 하므로 현재분사 carrying이 맞다. carry(동사원형)를 쓰면 문장 구조가 어긋난다 ← 정답
det.tip: 명사 + 현재분사(-ing): people carrying baskets(바구니를 든 사람들)

questions.passage: Curb cuts are a good example.  Without curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard time navigating the city.  Curb cuts eliminate barriers not only for wheelchair users but also for people moving heavy loads or riding bikes.
questions.stem: 위 글에서, 연석 경사로(curb cuts)가 없다면 도시를 이동하는 데 큰 어려움을 겪게 될 사람들을 가리키는 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (3단어, 영어로)

det.korean: 연석 경사로가 없을 때 어려움을 겪는 대상.
det.analysis: 본문 'Without curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard time navigating the city.'에서 연석 경사로가 없으면 도시를 다니는 데 어려움을 겪는 사람은 'people in wheelchairs(휠체어를 탄 사람들)'라고 밝혔다.
det.tip: Without curb cuts, people in wheelchairs ~에서 people in wheelchairs를 찾습니다.

questions.passage: Fortunately, various clever opening devices have been designed.  A lever-type door handle, which requires no firm grip or twisting, is also an example that reflects this characteristic of universal design.  A door with a lever-type door handle can be opened using an elbow or a closed hand, which benefits people carrying baskets as well as those with limited strength in their hands.
questions.stem: 위 글에서, 레버형 문손잡이(lever-type door handle)가 요구하지 않는다고 설명한 내용을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (5단어, 영어로)

det.korean: 레버형 문손잡이가 요구하지 않는 것.
det.analysis: 본문 'A lever-type door handle, which requires no firm grip or twisting'에서 레버형 손잡이가 요구하지 않는 것은 'no firm grip or twisting(꽉 쥐거나 비트는 동작이 필요 없음)'이라고 밝혔다.
det.tip: requires no firm grip or twisting에서 no firm grip or twisting을 찾습니다.

questions.passage: Information should be conveyed not just through written language but also through universal symbols and audio cues. For instance, when it comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is much easier when they can simply look for the universally __________ (recognize) restroom symbol rather than trying to interpret the local language.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.korean: recognized (과거분사).
det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'the universally ___ restroom symbol'에서 빈칸은 명사 symbol을 꾸미는 자리다. 기호(symbol)는 사람들에게 '인식되는' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사(-ed)로 바꿔야 한다. 따라서 recognize를 recognized로 고쳐 'the universally recognized restroom symbol(보편적으로 인식되는 화장실 기호)'가 된다.
det.tip: 명사를 꾸미며 '~되는(수동)' 의미이면 과거분사: recognized(인식되는)

questions.passage: What do you think good design is?  Some might assert good design makes products easy to use, while others might say good design is stylish or innovative.  There are even some who believe that good design should be as environmentally friendly as possible.  All of these are important elements of design.  However, there is a new idea called “universal design. ” This idea suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty looks and functions.  Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people and includes features that make it possible for them to access and use products without any barriers.  Now let’s take a look at how universal design is tackling the problem of limited access and reshaping the design of products and services.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글 전체를 아우르는 중심 소재.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 왼손잡이용 제품은 유연성을 보여 주는 하나의 예시일 뿐, 가격 비교는 글의 주제가 아님
✅ ② 유니버설 디자인이 다양한 사람의 요구를 고려하고, 유연성·접근성·적은 노력 등을 통해 누구나 장벽 없이 쓸 수 있게 한다는 것이 글 전체의 주제 ← 정답
❌ ③ 본문은 디자인이 '예쁜 겉모습을 넘어서야 한다'고 했으므로 미적 기법은 주제와 반대
❌ ④ 안전 규정 강화는 본문에 없는 내용
det.tip: diverse needs(다양한 요구) + without any barriers(장벽 없이)가 글 전체를 관통합니다.

ch: 왼손잡이용 제품이 오른손잡이용보다 더 비싼 이유
다양한 요구를 고려해 모두가 장벽 없이 사용하도록 하는 유니버설 디자인
제품을 더 아름답고 세련되게 보이도록 만드는 디자인 기법
공공건물의 안전 규정을 강화해야 하는 필요성

questions.passage: What do you think good design is?  Some might assert good design makes products easy to use, while others might say good design is stylish or innovative.  There are even some who believe that good design should be as environmentally friendly as possible.  All of these are important elements of design.  However, there is a new idea called “universal design. ” This idea suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty looks and functions.  Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people and includes features that make it possible for them to access and use products without any barriers.  Now let’s take a look at how universal design is tackling the problem of limited access and reshaping the design of products and services.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글쓴이가 전하려는 핵심 메시지.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문은 디자인이 예쁜 겉모습을 '넘어서야' 한다고 했으므로 외형 우선은 요지와 반대
❌ ② 왼손잡이용 제품은 유연성의 한 예시일 뿐, 그것만이 유니버설 디자인은 아님
✅ ③ 본문 'Universal design is beneficial to everyone.'처럼 유연성·접근성·적은 노력·정보 전달을 통해 모두에게 이로운 디자인을 지향한다는 것이 핵심 메시지 ← 정답
❌ ④ 복잡할수록 유용하다는 내용은 본문에 없으며 오히려 쉽게 쓰도록 하는 취지와 반대
det.tip: Universal design is beneficial to everyone(모두에게 이롭다)이 요지입니다.

ch: 디자인은 기능보다 외형이 훨씬 더 중요하다.
왼손잡이를 위한 제품만이 진정한 유니버설 디자인이다.
유니버설 디자인은 유연성·접근성·적은 노력·정보 전달을 통해 모두에게 이로운 디자인을 지향한다.
디자인이 복잡할수록 더 많은 사람에게 유용하다.

questions.passage: Universal design also ensures that an environment or product is accessible to everyone.  __________ regardless of who they are and what they’re capable of, and no one should be excluded.  Curb cuts are a good example.  Without curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard time navigating the city.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)

'누구나 그들이 누구이고 무엇을 할 수 있든 상관없이 디자인을 사용할 수 있어야 한다.'의 앞부분인 '누구나 디자인을 사용할 수 있어야 한다'를 영작하시오.

[조건]
(1) a, able, Anyone, be, design, should, to, use 를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: Anyone should be able to use a design
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- Anyone(주어): 누구나
- should be able to(~할 수 있어야 한다): 'be able to(~할 수 있다)' 앞에 조동사 should를 붙인 형태
- use a design(디자인을 사용하다): 동사 use + 목적어 a design
- 순서대로 놓으면 Anyone / should / be / able / to / use / a / design
det.tip: should be able to + 동사원형(~할 수 있어야 한다) / use a design(디자인을 사용하다)

questions.wa: Anyone should be able to use a design
